newsitem.title: USA: European concern over genetic beans not sound-USDA.
newsitem.headline: European concern over genetic beans not sound-USDA.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday that European concern over genetically- altered U.S. soybeans is worrisome, and is based on unsound science.
"It is a matter that is worrisome to me," he told reporters. "It worries us to see what I call unsound science out there ... shaping consumer attitudes."

A large retail grocery group in Europe threatened last week that consumers could boycott products made with soy unless U.S. exporters separate and label genetically modified soybeans developed by Monsanto and grown for the first time this year by U.S. farmers on a commercial basis.
Glickman said that since the European Union has officially approved the safety of the soybeans, the latest developments are not U.S. government related, but largely a consumer issue.
He said USDA officials are talking with export companies now about the issue, but said it is basically an issue for the companies to work out.
"The companies are beginning to struggle with this matter ... this is a real problem for the companies," Glickman said.
Glickman said the USDA is watching closely the upcoming EU decision on whether to approve genetically-engineered corn.
"It could become a trade issue," he said.

Glickman said that although EU action on corn, and European concern over the soybeans, could impact U.S. exports, he does not think it will become a "practical problem" because the EU needs U.S. corn and soy products.
The Agriculture Secretary said the USDA is providing scientific information to the EU to help them come to a decision to approve gene-altered corn, and help reduce consumer fears on the new soybeans.
